source_refs.note: The unnumbered topic Spin Quantum Number (s), printed page 32, with the spin figure printed as Figure 2.4.

blocks.text: Electrons are thought of as spinning around their own axes, as the Earth does. According to electromagnetic theory a spinning charge generates a magnetic field, and this motion makes an electron behave like a magnet. There are two possible spinning motions, clockwise and anticlockwise, so to take the spin into account a fourth quantum number, the electron spin quantum number s, is introduced, with the values +1/2 and -1/2. The clockwise spin is represented by an arrow pointing upwards and the other by an arrow pointing downwards. Each orbital can accommodate at most two electrons, provided the two have opposite spins. So it takes three quantum numbers to describe an orbital, but a fourth to tell apart the two electrons that can occupy it.

blocks.title: Did you know
blocks.text: In the nth principal quantum number there are n subshells consisting of n squared orbitals with a maximum of 2n squared electrons.

blocks.prompt: Two electrons occupy the 1s orbital of helium. Write the four quantum numbers of each and say what differs.
blocks.explanation: Both have n = 1, l = 0 and m = 0, because they are in the same orbital. They differ only in spin: one has s = +1/2 and the other s = -1/2, so their spins are opposite, which is what lets two electrons share one orbital.

items: The spin quantum number s is +1/2 (arrow up) or -1/2 (arrow down); a spinning electron acts like a magnet.
An orbital holds at most two electrons, and only with opposite spins; three quantum numbers fix the orbital, the fourth the electron.
